title: Order edits failing
summary: Order edits began failing at 13:35 UTC after the orders-service v2.15.0 deploy (chg:2501) introduced a new PATCH /v1/orders amendment endpoint. The endpoint’s validation code dereferences `order.limitPrice` without a null guard, causing a NullPointerException that surfaces as 500 errors on the edge‑gateway (HYP‑1, confidence 0.86). The critic accepted HYP‑1 as the conclusive cause. A secondary data‑issue hypothesis (pre‑existing NULL limitPrice values) was not ruled out but lacks direct evidence (no DB query confirming NULL rows).

hypothesis.mechanism: The v2.15.0 deploy added a new PATCH /v1/orders amendment endpoint. Its validation code (AmendOrderHandler.validate) reads order.limitPrice and dereferences it without a null guard. When the endpoint is invoked on any order, a NullPointerException is thrown, producing 500 responses that propagate to edge-gateway.
predictions: Adding a null check for order.limitPrice in the amendment handler will eliminate the NPE and return error_rate to baseline.
Edge‑gateway 5xx on /v1/orders will drop to baseline once the fix is deployed.

hypothesis.mechanism: Existing open market orders have limitPrice = NULL. The previous edit flow never inspected limitPrice, so they succeeded. The new amendment endpoint (introduced by the same deploy) validates limitPrice and crashes when it encounters the pre‑existing NULL values.
predictions: A one‑time backfill that sets a default limitPrice (or marks market orders as non‑editable) will stop the NPE without code change.
If the amendment endpoint is disabled via feature flag, the error rate returns to baseline even though the NULL data remains.

objections.detail: HYP‑1 (code regression) fully accounts for the observed NPEs and error‑rate spike. Until HYP‑2 is either confirmed (by showing NULL limitPrice rows) or falsified, it remains an alternative that has not been excluded.

No evidence has been gathered that any open order records have limitPrice = NULL. The tools can reveal this by querying orders‑service logs for the validation path or by inspecting the orders table, but neither has been done.

facts.statement: orders-service throws NullPointerException on PATCH /v1/orders because order.limitPrice is null in AmendOrderHandler.validate (first seen 13:33:01 UTC, 413 occurrences).
orders-service error_rate spikes to a mean of 0.0185 (baseline 0.0021) with a peak of 0.0663 between 13:33‑13:58 UTC.
edge-gateway logs 379 upstream 500 responses from orders-service on route /v1/orders starting at 13:34:05 UTC.
postgres-orders reports only checkpoint‑frequency warnings; CPU, query latency p99, and active connections stay within baseline.
orders-service latency (p50 mean 44 ms, p99 mean 260 ms) is unchanged versus baseline.
orders-service v2.15.0 (adds amendment endpoint) deployed at 13:31:20 UTC, two minutes before the first NPE.
The change census for the six call‑chain services returns exactly two changes in the window: chg:2497 (auth-service config) and chg:2501 (orders-service deploy).
orders-service deploy chg:2501 at 2026-10-05T13:31:20Z released v2.15.0 adding an order amendment endpoint (diff +296/-41).
The auth-service timeout change (chg:2497) only affects session idle expiration and cannot directly cause order‑edit failures.

assumptions.reason: The stack trace shows the NPE originates in AmendOrderHandler.validate accessing limitPrice.

assumptions.statement: The v2.15.0 deploy introduced the validation code path with no feature‑flag gating observed.
assumptions.reason: Change census records only the deploy (chg:2501) and no flag toggle in the window.

assumptions.statement: Some open orders in the system legitimately have limitPrice = NULL (e.g., market orders).
assumptions.reason: Domain knowledge: market orders are stored without a limit price; the previous edit path did not read this field.

assumptions.statement: The prior edit flow did not read limitPrice, so the NULL values were harmless until the new endpoint was added.
assumptions.reason: Only the new amendment handler accesses limitPrice, as indicated by the NPE location.

actions.description: Disable the new amendment endpoint (e.g., via feature flag) or roll back orders-service to v2.14.3 to stop the 5xx error burst immediately.
actions.rationale: The NPE occurs on every edit request; turning off the faulty code path restores order‑edit functionality while a permanent fix is prepared.

actions.description: Add a null check for `order.limitPrice` in `AmendOrderHandler.validate` (or make the field non‑nullable with a default) and deploy the corrected version.
actions.rationale: Directly eliminates the NPE identified in the logs (OBS‑7) and matches the prediction that error_rate will return to baseline.

actions.description: Introduce unit/integration tests that exercise the amendment endpoint with market orders lacking a limitPrice, and add a pre‑deploy static‑analysis rule to flag missing null guards on newly added fields.
actions.rationale: Prevents regression of the same null‑dereference pattern in future endpoint additions.

actions.description: Query the orders table (or orders‑service logs) for any open orders where `limitPrice` IS NULL to confirm or falsify HYP‑2.
actions.rationale: The critic flagged the lack of evidence for existing NULL limitPrice rows; confirming this would clarify whether a data back‑fill is also required.

actions.description: Obtain the full source diff for commit e4a91c2 (orders‑service v2.15.0) and verify the exact validation logic and any feature‑flag gating.
actions.rationale: Gap‑4 and Gap‑7 indicate the diff is not in the tooling; seeing the code confirms the null‑check omission and flag state.

Was the amendment endpoint gated behind a feature flag, and if so, when was the flag enabled relative to the deploy?
Are there any untracked config or infra changes for the involved services during the incident window (Gap‑6)?
